verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between Riboflavin and Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, mediated through azelaic acid. Riboflavin is directly linked to MM96L, which is a target of azelaic acid. Azelaic acid, in turn, targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. This pathway implies a possible indirect interaction where Riboflavin may influence the activity of MM96L, which then affects the transport of organic anions, including those involving Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The evidence supports a mechanistic link through a chain of targets, though the exact nature of the interaction between Riboflavin and MM96L remains unclear. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as it is based on a single score, and further experimental validation would be needed to confirm the direct involvement of Riboflavin in this process.
